entry.title: Air Fryer Chicken Time and Temperature Chart
entry.summary: Air fryer chicken time and temperature chart for breast, thighs, wings, tenders and drumsticks, with the 165°F / 74°C rule and frozen times.
entry.content:
Chicken is the food people most want to cook in an air fryer, and the food they most often get wrong. The window between juicy and sawdust is narrow, and it moves depending on how thick the piece is and whether it still has a bone.

So this chart gives ranges you can start from. The number that decides whether dinner is safe is not on this page at all — it is the one your thermometer reads.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. Wattage and basket size change the clock, but 165°F / 74°C does not change.

Why time alone is unreliable for chicken

A 6-ounce breast and an 8-ounce breast look almost identical in the basket. One finishes in 14 minutes and the other needs 20. Bone-in pieces cook slower near the bone. A crowded basket slows everything down because the air cannot circulate.

An air fryer also browns the outside long before the inside is done. That is why a piece can look perfect, smell perfect and still be undercooked in the center. Color, juices and firmness are all guesses. A thermometer is a measurement.

Here is what the measurement has to say, according to USDA:

Poultry and related foodsSafe internal temperature
Chicken breast, thighs, wings, drumsticks, whole chicken165°F / 74°C
Ground chicken and ground turkey165°F / 74°C
Breaded chicken, fresh or frozen165°F / 74°C
Chicken leftovers, reheated165°F / 74°C

Note what is missing: there is no rest time that substitutes for temperature, and there is no cut of chicken where 160°F / 71°C is acceptable. Poultry is 165°F / 74°C across the board. Probe the thickest part, away from bone, fat and the pan's hot spot.

Air fryer chicken chart: thawed chicken

Times assume a preheated basket, one layer, and pieces of similar size. Add 2–4 minutes if your machine runs cool or the basket is full.

CutTemperatureTimeNotes
Chicken breast, boneless skinless375°F / 190°C18–22 minFlip at halfway, 165°F / 74°C
Chicken breast, bone-in skin-on380°F / 193°C24–28 minProbe near bone, 165°F / 74°C
Chicken thighs, bone-in skin-on380°F / 193°C25–30 minSkin side up first
Chicken thighs, boneless skinless380°F / 193°C18–22 minDo not overcook, they dry out
Chicken wings, split380°F / 193°C22–26 minShake every 8 min
Chicken tenders380°F / 193°C10–12 minShake once, 165°F / 74°C
Chicken drumsticks380°F / 193°C22–26 minTurn at halfway
Whole small chicken, 3–4 lb350°F / 177°C50–60 minCheck at 45 min, 165°F / 74°C

A whole chicken only works in a large basket, and only if there is space around it for air to move. If the bird touches the element guard, spatchcock it and cook it in two halves instead — 35–45 minutes at 380°F / 193°C, checked at the thickest part of the thigh.

Air fryer chicken chart: from frozen

Frozen breaded chicken is designed to go straight into the basket. Raw frozen chicken pieces are not a good idea: the outside overcooks while the center thaws.

Frozen chickenTemperatureTimeNotes
Nuggets400°F / 205°C10–12 minShake at halfway
Wings, breaded380°F / 193°C20–24 minShake every 8 min
Wings, unbreaded380°F / 193°C24–28 minShake twice
Tenders, breaded390°F / 199°C12–15 minFlip at halfway
Chicken fries400°F / 205°C10–12 minSingle layer
Popcorn chicken400°F / 205°C9–12 minShake at 5 min
Raw frozen breast, thin370°F / 188°C22–28 minOnly if labeled cook from frozen

Frozen versus thawed: what actually changes

Thawed chicken gives you more control. You can season it through, pound it to an even thickness and predict the time. Frozen breaded chicken gives you speed and a crisp coating, at the cost of not knowing the exact internal temperature until you probe it.

If you are cooking raw chicken you froze yourself, thaw it in the refrigerator — never on the counter. A thin breast thaws overnight; a whole bird needs closer to 24 hours. Once thawed, treat it like fresh chicken and use the thawed chart.

For anything breaded, skip the oil. The coating is already formulated to crisp, and adding oil makes it greasy and soft.

Five mistakes with air fryer chicken

  1. Going by the clock. A range tells you when to start checking, not when to stop.
  2. Probing the bone. Bone heats differently and reads high. Aim for the thickest flesh.
  3. Overcrowding. Two layers of chicken means uneven cooking and a cold spot in the middle.
  4. Skipping the rest. Five minutes on a board lets the juices settle. It does not replace reaching 165°F / 74°C.
  5. Cranking the heat to save time. Above 400°F / 205°C the outside burns before the center catches up.

Frequently asked questions

What temperature do I cook chicken in an air fryer? Most cuts do well at 375–400°F / 190–205°C. Whatever you choose, the chicken must reach 165°F / 74°C in the thickest part before you serve it.

How long does chicken breast take in an air fryer? 18–22 minutes at 375°F / 190°C for a boneless breast, flipped at halfway. A thick breast may need the longer end; a thin one may finish sooner. Check at 16 minutes.

Can I cook frozen raw chicken in an air fryer? Only if the package says it is formulated to cook from frozen. Otherwise thaw it in the refrigerator first. Raw frozen pieces cook unevenly and are hard to verify.

Is 160°F / 71°C good enough for chicken? No. USDA sets 165°F / 74°C for all poultry, including ground chicken. If your thermometer reads 160°F / 71°C, keep cooking and probe again.

Do I need oil on chicken? For skin-on pieces, a light rub helps browning. Breaded frozen chicken needs none.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Chicken Wings: Time and Temperature Chart
entry.summary: Air fryer chicken wings time and temperature chart for fresh and frozen wings, with sauce timing, crisp finishes and the 165°F / 74°C rule.
entry.content:
Wings are the food the air fryer was practically made for: circulating hot air crisps the skin all over, with far less oil than deep frying and no oven splatter. The catch is that wings carry a lot of skin and fat, so they can look glossy and done while the joint is still undercooked.

This chart gives starting times for fresh and frozen wings, plus the timing that keeps sauce from burning. The number that ends the cook is not on this page — it is what your thermometer reads in the thickest part of the drumette.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. Wattage, basket size and crowding change the clock, but 165°F / 74°C does not change.

The rule that matters most for wings

Wings are poultry, and poultry has one internal temperature under USDA rules. There is no sauce, rub or cooking style that changes it:

PoultrySafe internal temperature
Fresh or thawed chicken wings165°F / 74°C
Frozen chicken wings, cooked from frozen165°F / 74°C
Breaded chicken wings, fresh or frozen165°F / 74°C
Cooked wings reheated later165°F / 74°C

Probe the thickest part of the drumette, keeping the thermometer tip away from the bone. If the largest wing reads 165°F / 74°C, the smaller ones around it are done too.

Air fryer chicken wings chart: fresh

Times assume a preheated basket, a single layer and wings of similar size. Shake the basket every 8 minutes so the skin renders evenly.

Wing styleTemperatureTimeNotes
Split wings, drums and flats380°F / 193°C22–26 minShake every 8 minutes
Whole wings, tips attached380°F / 193°C24–28 minFlip at halfway
Dry-rubbed wings380°F / 193°C22–26 minRubs with sugar darken faster
Breaded fresh wings380°F / 193°C20–24 minSingle layer, light oil spray
Cornstarch-dusted wings380°F / 193°C22–26 minShake once more than usual

Start checking at the 20 minute mark. A range tells you when to begin checking, not when to stop. Wings hold heat well, so a 3 minute rest before saucing keeps them hot and juicy.

Crispy finish and sauce timing

The order of sauce and heat decides whether wings end crisp or soggy. The safest sequence: cook fully, sauce hot, serve immediately. If you want a lacquered glaze, use the short finish in the table below.

StepTemperatureTimeNotes
Extra-crisp finish, plain wings400°F / 205°C3–5 minAfter the main cook, watch closely
Glaze during the last minutes380°F / 193°C2–3 minThin glaze only; sugars burn fast
Buffalo sauce after cookingOff heatToss while hotBest crust, no burning risk
Butter-based sauce after cookingOff heatToss and serveSit too long and skin softens

A full buffalo treatment — sauce during cooking at high heat — is the most common way wings burn in an air fryer. The sauce contains sugar and butter, and both scorch above 400°F / 205°C. Sauce after the cook, or glaze for only the last 2–3 minutes.

Air fryer chicken wings chart: frozen

Frozen wings cook well from frozen because the coating is designed for it. No thawing, no oil, no rinsing.

Frozen wingsTemperatureTimeNotes
Breaded frozen wings380°F / 193°C20–24 minShake every 8 minutes
Unbreaded frozen wings380°F / 193°C24–28 minShake twice during the cook
Frozen glazed wings380°F / 193°C20–24 minFoil under the basket catches drips

Because frozen wings start cold in the center, the thermometer matters even more. Breaded frozen wings frequently need the full range before the thickest drumette reaches 165°F / 74°C.

Five mistakes with air fryer wings

  1. Saucing before the skin crisps. Wet sauce on raw skin steams it; sauce after cooking keeps the crust.
  2. Crowding the basket. Two layers means steamed wings in the middle and burnt wings on the edge.
  3. Judging by color. Skin can be deep golden while the joint is undercooked; only the thermometer knows.
  4. Skipping the shakes. Wings sitting in rendered fat cook unevenly — shake every 8 minutes.
  5. Cranking past 400°F / 205°C. Fat spatters onto the element and the skin burns before the collagen softens.

Frequently asked questions

Can wings be pink near the bone and still be done? Yes. Bone marrow can tint the meat pink even when the wing is fully cooked. Wings are safe when the thickest part of the drumette reaches 165°F / 74°C, regardless of color.

Do wings need oil in the air fryer? Plain wings benefit from a light spray for even browning; breaded wings need none, since the coating already contains fat.

How do I keep buffalo sauce from burning? Toss the wings in sauce after cooking, while they are hot. For a baked-on glaze, brush a thin layer and hold at 380°F / 193°C for only 2–3 minutes.

Why are my wings tough instead of crisp? The heat is too high for too long. Skin crisps between 380°F / 193°C and 400°F / 205°C; the collagen in the joint needs time at temperature, not more temperature.

Can I cook then hold wings for a party? Cook fully, rest 5 minutes, then hold in a 200°F / 93°C oven or warm setting for up to 30 minutes. Sauce at serving time, not before.

Wings reward patience more than power. Cook at 380°F / 193°C, shake often, verify with a thermometer at the thickest joint, and sauce at the end — that sequence gives crisp skin and a safe, juicy interior every time.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

  2. Skipping the preheat. Three minutes of preheat is the difference between crisp and pale.
  3. Too little oil on vegetables. A dry surface burns before the inside cooks.
  4. Not shaking. Every 8–10 minutes for anything in a pile.
  5. Going by the clock instead of a thermometer. Especially with chicken.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to preheat an air fryer? For anything you want browned, yes — about 3 minutes at the cooking temperature. For reheating and for delicate items, it matters less.

Should I line the basket with foil or parchment? Only if the liner is perforated or the food sits above it. A solid liner blocks the airflow the machine depends on and can be a fire risk if it lifts into the element.

Is an air fryer the same as a convection oven? Functionally close: a small, fast convection oven. The difference is proximity — the element is inches from the food, which is why times are shorter.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Corn on the Cob: Times for Husked, In-Husk and Frozen
entry.summary: Air fryer corn on the cob times for husked, in-husk and frozen corn, with butter and oil handling and a note on reheating leftover corn safely.
entry.content:
Corn on the cob is the easiest side an air fryer makes. There is no pot of boiling water, no big kettle to drain, and the kernels come out with browned, slightly chewy spots that boiled corn never gets.

It is also the one food on this site with no internal temperature to hit. Corn is a vegetable, and vegetables have no USDA safe internal temperature.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer for meat and poultry. For corn, use the clock and your eyes, and remember that wattage and basket size change the time.

There is no safe internal temperature for corn

This matters because it is a common question. USDA publishes safe internal temperatures for meat, poultry, fish, eggs and reheated leftovers, not for vegetables. Corn has no target number, so anyone quoting one for the kernels is inventing it.

What corn does have is a doneness you can see. The kernels turn bright yellow, some of them brown at the tips, and a kernel pressed with a fork gives slightly. If the kernels look pale and flat, they need more time.

The exception is leftover corn. Once corn has been cooked and refrigerated, reheating it puts it under the standard for reheated food, which is 165°F / 74°C.

CornSafe internal temperature
Fresh or frozen corn on the cob, first cookNone — vegetables have no USDA target
Corn reheated from leftovers165°F / 74°C

Husked versus in-husk

Husked corn cooks faster and browns more. In-husk corn steams inside its own wrapper and comes out juicier, with a milder flavor and no browned spots.

PreparationTemperatureTimeNotes
Husked, whole cob400°F / 205°C10–14 minTurn at halfway
Husked, cut in halves400°F / 205°C8–11 minFaster, more surface
Husked, kernels on foil390°F / 199°C10–13 minKeep the foil loose
In husk, whole cob400°F / 205°C15–20 minSoak 10 min first
In husk, husk pulled back400°F / 205°C12–16 minSilk removed, husk as handle
Frozen, husked, whole cob400°F / 205°C14–18 minNo thawing needed
Frozen, in husk390°F / 199°C18–22 minAdd 2–3 min to fresh
Canned or drained kernels390°F / 199°C8–11 minSpread in a single layer

For in-husk corn, pull the husk down without removing it, strip the silk, then pull the husk back up over the kernels. The husk becomes a handle and a shield at the same time. Soak the cob in cold water for ten minutes first so the husk does not scorch.

Frozen corn on the cob goes in straight from the freezer. There is no need to thaw it, and thawing it first only adds water to the basket.

Butter, oil and seasoning

Corn has almost no fat of its own, so something has to carry the seasoning and help the kernels brown.

For husked corn, brush or rub each cob with a thin coat of oil or melted butter before it goes in, and season with salt and pepper. A light coat is enough. Too much butter pools in the basket, smokes, and leaves the kernels greasy rather than browned.

For in-husk corn, put the fat inside. Peel the husk back, brush the kernels, add salt, and close the husk again. The husk traps the butter against the corn.

Butter burns at a lower temperature than oil, and an air fryer moves hot air directly over the surface. If you want butter flavor without scorching, cook the corn with oil and brush it with melted butter after it comes out of the basket. That gives you browning from the oil and butter flavor that never hit the element.

Cold butter straight from the refrigerator does not spread. Melt it, or soften it first.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. Corn has no internal temperature, but any meat you cook alongside it does.

Common mistakes with air fryer corn

  1. Peeling every husk by reflex. In-husk corn is juicier and needs no foil.
  2. Soaking for hours. Ten minutes is enough to keep the husk from burning.
  3. Drowning the cob in butter. It smokes and pools; a thin coat browns better.
  4. Stacking cobs. Two layers means the bottom cobs steam and stay pale.
  5. Leaving the silk on. Silk that stays on the cob does not soften, it just sticks to the kernels.

Reheating leftover corn

Cooked corn on the cob keeps in the refrigerator for three to five days. Reheat it in the air fryer at 350°F / 177°C for 4–6 minutes, turning once.

For loose kernels, spread them in a single layer at 350°F / 177°C for 4–5 minutes. They will not brown much, because they are already cooked, and that is fine.

Reheated leftovers are held to the 165°F / 74°C standard, so reheat corn until it is steaming hot rather than merely warm. If you are reheating corn along with leftover meat, the meat needs its own check: 165°F / 74°C for poultry and any reheated leftovers.

Frequently asked questions

How long does corn on the cob take in an air fryer?

10–14 minutes at 400°F / 205°C for husked corn, and 15–20 minutes at 400°F / 205°C when the husk is left on. Frozen cobs need 14–18 minutes without thawing.

Do I need to soak corn before air frying it?

Only if you leave the husk on. Ten minutes in cold water keeps the husk from scorching before the kernels are done. Husked corn needs no soaking.

Should I wrap corn in foil in the air fryer?

No. Foil blocks the moving air that browns the kernels, and loose foil can lift into the heating element. Cook the corn directly in the basket.

Can I cook corn and other food at the same time?

Only if the times match. Corn needs 10–14 minutes of its own, so give it the basket first or add it late. Cook meat separately and check it with a thermometer.

Is canned corn worth air frying?

Yes, for a quick side. Drain it well, pat it dry, spread it in a single layer, and give it 8–11 minutes at 390°F / 199°C. Wet corn steams instead of browning.

The short version

Husked corn: 400°F / 205°C for 10–14 minutes, turned once, with a thin coat of oil. In-husk corn: soaked ten minutes, then 15–20 minutes at 400°F / 205°C. Frozen cobs: straight in for 14–18 minutes. No internal temperature is needed for the corn itself, but reheat any leftovers to 165°F / 74°C.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Crab Cakes: Time and Temperature for Golden Cakes
entry.summary: Air fryer crab cake times for fresh and frozen cakes, with 400°F / 205°C settings, the 145°F / 63°C internal rule and the chilling rule.
entry.content:
Crab cakes are the appetizer the air fryer handles with the least effort: no pan of oil, no flipping fragile cakes in a skillet — the moving air browns both sides while the cake holds its shape on the basket.

The two rules that matter: chill the cakes before cooking so they hold, and verify the internal temperature of the crab.

Times vary by appliance model. Cake size, filler amount and crowding change the clock, but 145°F / 63°C does not change.

The rule for crab

Crab is shellfish, and shellfish under FDA guidance cooks to the same standard as fish:

Crab cakeSafe internal temperatureRest
Fresh crab cakes145°F / 63°C—
Frozen crab cakes, cooked from frozen145°F / 63°C—
Leftover crab cakes, reheated145°F / 63°C—

Probe the center of the thickest cake. Crab cakes are delicate — probe from the side at an angle so the cake does not split.

Air fryer crab cake chart

Chill the shaped cakes at least 30 minutes before cooking — a warm cake sags in the basket. A light spray of oil on both sides gives the golden crust.

CakeTemperatureTimeNotes
Fresh, 3 oz cakes400°F / 205°C8–10 minFlip once, carefully
Fresh, 4 oz cakes400°F / 205°C10–12 minCheck at 9 min
Frozen, store-bought400°F / 205°C10–13 minNo thawing, single layer
Mini cakes, 1.5 oz400°F / 205°C6–8 minShake once
Extra-golden finish425°F / 218°C1–2 minWatch closely, last minutes

The flip is the one delicate moment: a wide, thin spatula and one confident turn at halfway. The cakes firm as they cook, so the second half of the cook is safe to move.

The mix: filler and binder

A good crab cake is mostly crab — the filler holds, the crab stars. The standard ratio is one egg and a quarter cup of breadcrumbs per pound of crab, with mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire and Old Bay seasoning.

ElementAmount per pound of crabWhy
Egg1The binder that sets in the heat
Breadcrumbs1/4 cupHolds moisture and shape
Mayonnaise2 tbspRichness that keeps the cake tender
Old Bay1 tspThe signature seasoning

Too much filler turns the cake into a breadcrumb patty; too little and it falls apart. The ratio above is the balance that holds together and still tastes of crab.

Five mistakes with air fryer crab cakes

  1. Cooking warm, freshly mixed cakes. They sag in the basket; chill 30+ minutes first.
  2. Flipping with a thin, quick wrist. A wide spatula and one confident turn at halfway.
  3. Overcooking past 145°F / 63°C. Crab turns rubbery fast; pull at temperature.
  4. Too much filler. One egg and a quarter cup of crumbs per pound — the crab should star.
  5. Overcrowding. Cakes touching steam each other; one layer with air between.

Frequently asked questions

How long do crab cakes take in an air fryer? 8–10 minutes at 400°F / 205°C for 3-ounce cakes, flipped once at halfway. Frozen ones need 10–13 minutes; mini cakes 6–8 minutes.

What temperature should crab cakes be inside? 145°F / 63°C in the center — the FDA standard for shellfish, the same as fish.

Do I need to thaw frozen crab cakes? No — straight into the basket at 400°F / 205°C for 10–13 minutes. Verify the center of the thickest one.

Why did my crab cakes fall apart? They were warm from the mix or had too little binder. Chill the shaped cakes 30+ minutes, and keep the ratio at one egg plus a quarter cup of crumbs per pound.

How do I reheat crab cakes? 350°F / 177°C for 5–7 minutes keeps them tender; higher heat turns the crab rubbery. The reheated center should reach 145°F / 63°C.

Crab cakes reward chilling and restraint: 30 minutes cold, one careful flip, pulled at 145°F / 63°C. The air fryer gives the golden crust of pan-frying with none of the oil.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Desserts Chart (Cookies, Cakes and More)
entry.summary: Air fryer desserts chart with times and temperatures for cookies, mug cakes, brownies, cinnamon rolls, donuts, baked apples, s'mores and churros.
entry.content:
Dessert is the hardest thing to cook in an air fryer, and it is not close. A savoury dish tells you when it is done with colour and a thermometer. A cookie tells you nothing until you bite it.

The heating element sits inches from the food, the fan pushes dry air across the surface, and the basket is small. Cakes and cookies set on the outside while the middle is still batter. This is the category where a chart is a starting point and nothing more.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. For desserts the thermometer measures the air, not the food: there is no safe internal temperature for a cookie. Use a toothpick.

The rule that matters more than any number on this page

There is no safe internal temperature for dessert. USDA internal-temperature guidance covers meat, poultry, eggs and leftovers, not cake batter, so anyone quoting you "the internal temperature of a brownie" is inventing a number.

That leaves you two checks that actually work:

  • Start checking early. If the chart says 15–18 min, look at 12 min. The last three minutes are where desserts go from underdone to ruined.
  • Use the toothpick test. Insert a wooden toothpick or skewer into the centre and pull it out. A few moist crumbs are done. Wet batter is not.

Cakes with eggs still need to be fully set, because raw egg is a food-safety issue in the same way it is in any other dish. If the centre is liquid, keep cooking in 1–2 min steps.

Air fryer desserts chart

Temperatures are given as ranges on purpose. A 1500-watt basket and a 1800-watt oven with a small drawer behave differently, and dark non-stick pans bake faster than pale metal ones.

DessertTemperatureTimeCheck
Cookies from refrigerated dough320–340°F / 160–171°C8–11 minEdges set, centre soft, toothpick
Cookies from homemade dough310–330°F / 154–166°C7–10 minPale gold edge, toothpick
Mug cake in an 8 oz mug350°F / 177°C12–15 minToothpick, top springs back
Small cake in a 6 in pan300–320°F / 149–160°C18–24 minToothpick, sides pull away
Brownies in ramekins320°F / 160°C18–22 minMoist crumbs, never wet batter
Cinnamon rolls from a can325–340°F / 163–171°C12–16 minGolden top, centre set
Donuts from canned biscuits350–370°F / 177–188°C5–8 minGolden both sides, firm to touch
Baked apples, halved and cored350°F / 177°C15–20 minKnife slides in with no resistance
S'mores, assembled350°F / 177°C3–5 minMarshmallow browned, chocolate soft
Churros, piped or frozen375°F / 190°C8–12 minDeep gold, crisp shell, dry centre

Check the earliest time in every range. If the item is not there yet, add 1–2 min and look again. There is no dish on that table that benefits from guessing.

Here is what each check is really telling you, so you can judge a dessert the chart does not list.

What you seeWhat it meansWhat to do
Toothpick comes out with wet batterCentre is still liquidCook 2 min more and check again
Toothpick comes out with moist crumbsDoneTake it out and cool on a rack
Top is dark but the centre wobblesHeat too high, pan too deepDrop 25°F / 15°C and add time next batch
Edges crisp, middle rawBasket crowded or pan too fullFewer pieces, single layer
Bottom pale and doughyBasket not preheatedPreheat 2–3 min before the next batch

How to run each dessert without wrecking it

Refrigerated cookie dough. Slice it cold, keep 1 inch between pieces and cook in a single layer. Dough that warms up on the counter spreads into one sheet. Cold dough holds its shape. If you use a parchment liner, cut it so air still moves and weight it with the dough.

Mug cakes. A straight-sided mug heats more evenly than a wide shallow one. Fill it no more than two-thirds, because the batter climbs. Ceramic holds heat longer than silicone, so it may need the longer end of the range.

Small cakes and brownies. Use the smallest pan that fits with space around it. A 6-inch round pan or two ramekins beat one deep tin, because the centre is closer to the moving air. Lower the temperature rather than the time when the top darkens too fast.

Cinnamon rolls. One layer, spiral side up, with a gap between rolls so they can expand. Frost them after they come out, never before, or the icing slides off and burns.

Donuts from canned biscuits. Flatten each biscuit into a ring, cut a hole with a bottle cap or your thumb, and cook in a single layer. They firm up fast, so check at 5 min. Toss in cinnamon sugar while hot so it sticks.

Baked apples. Halved apples cook more evenly than whole ones, which take far longer than most baskets can handle. A firm apple keeps its shape; a soft one collapses into sauce.

S'mores. Assemble on a small foil or parchment square for easy removal. Watch them the whole time. Marshmallows go from toasted to black in well under a minute at 350°F / 177°C.

Churros. Piping wet dough straight into a hot basket is messy and it spreads. Pipe onto parchment, freeze for 20 min until firm, then cook. Frozen churros also hold their ridges, which is the whole point of a churro.

Cooling and storage

Most air-fried desserts firm up as they cool, because the structure keeps setting for several minutes after the heat stops. A cookie that looks underdone at 8 min may be perfect at 12 min. Take it out, wait 5 min on a rack, then judge it.

Cool anything you are storing on a rack, not in the basket. Trapped steam under the basket turns a crisp edge soft. Store covered at room temperature for a day or two, or refrigerate anything with a cream, custard or fruit filling and eat it within 2–3 days. Leftover baked goods from the refrigerator are eaten cold, not reheated, and any dish you do reheat should reach 165°F / 74°C.

Five mistakes with air fryer desserts

  1. Using the savoury temperature. A 400°F / 205°C basket burns sugar and chocolate before the centre sets. Drop the heat and add time.
  2. Skipping the preheat. Cold air and cold dough give you a flat, pale cookie. Two to three minutes of preheat is enough.
  3. Crowding the basket. Two layers of dough fuse into a slab and the middle stays raw.
  4. Trusting the timer over the toothpick. Times vary by model more than any other category, and this one has no thermometer backup.
  5. Opening the drawer every minute. It drops the temperature each time. Check at the earliest time in the range, then leave it alone.

Frequently asked questions

Can I bake cookies in an air fryer? Yes, at 310–340°F / 154–171°C for 7–11 min depending on the dough. Keep them in one layer and check two to three minutes before the end of the range.

What temperature do I use for an air fryer cake? Lower than you expect, around 300–320°F / 149–160°C, because the element is close to the top of the batter. The centre sets before the crust darkens at that heat.

Why is my air fryer cake raw in the middle? The pan is too deep or too full, or the temperature is too high. Use a shallower pan, fill it two-thirds, lower the heat and give it more time.

How do I know when a dessert is done without a thermometer? Use the toothpick test. Moist crumbs mean done, wet batter means keep going. There is no internal-temperature standard for baked desserts.

Can I cook frozen cookie dough straight from the freezer? Yes, and it is easier than thawed dough because it spreads less. Add 1–3 min to the range and check at the earliest time.

The short version

Air fryer desserts need lower heat, more patience and an early check. Use a toothpick, not a thermometer, and treat 300–340°F / 149–171°C as your baking zone. Cookies, brownies and cinnamon rolls work well in small batches. Anything with a wet batter in a deep pan does not.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Egg Rolls: Fresh and Frozen Times
entry.summary: Air fryer egg roll times for frozen and homemade rolls, with the crisp-wrapper rules, filling safety and the oil-spray question answered.
entry.content:
Egg rolls are the appetizer the air fryer handles best: hot air crisps the wrapper on every side with a fraction of the oil of deep frying, and there is no pot of hot oil to manage. The difference between crisp and soggy is almost entirely preparation and one temperature decision.

This chart covers frozen and homemade rolls, the wrapper rules and filling safety.

Times vary by appliance model. Wrapper thickness, filling moisture and basket crowding change the clock — watch the first batch.

Air fryer egg rolls chart

Frozen rolls go straight into the basket — no thawing. Thawing softens the wrapper and it turns leathery instead of crisp.

Egg rollsTemperatureTimeNotes
Frozen, standard380°F / 193°C12–15 minFlip at halfway
Frozen, mini380°F / 193°C9–12 minShake once
Homemade, cooked filling380°F / 193°C8–12 minLight oil spray
Homemade, frozen on a tray380°F / 193°C12–15 minFreeze solid first
Spring rolls, thin wrapper380°F / 193°C8–10 minWatch closely, thin skins

The flip at halfway matters more for egg rolls than for most foods: the basket-side wrapper stays pale and chewy without one confident turn.

The wrapper rules for homemade rolls

Three habits decide whether a homemade wrapper crisps:

  • Cooked, cooled filling. Hot filling steams the wrapper from inside and softens it before the cook begins. Cool the filling completely, then wrap.
  • Do not overfill. A stuffed roll splits at the seam and leaks into the basket. Two tablespoons of filling per standard wrapper is the reliable amount.
  • Seal with a flour paste. A corner of wrapper sealed with flour-and-water paste holds through the cook; a dry seam opens.

Lightly spray the wrapped rolls with oil — the wrapper itself carries none, and a thin coat is what turns golden. Skip the spray and the wrapper browns patchy and pale.

Filling safety

Most egg roll fillings are cooked before wrapping — pork, cabbage, mushrooms all sauté first. Two rules keep that safe:

FillingThe rule
Pork fillingCook the pork to 160°F / 71°C before wrapping
Poultry fillingCook the chicken to 165°F / 74°C before wrapping
Vegetable-only fillingCook and cool before wrapping

The short air fryer cook browns the wrapper — it is not long enough to cook raw meat inside a wrapped roll. Cook the filling fully, cool it, then wrap.

Five mistakes with air fryer egg rolls

  1. Thawing frozen rolls. A soft wrapper turns leathery; cook them straight from frozen.
  2. Hot filling in a fresh wrapper. Steam softens the skin before the cook starts; cool first.
  3. Overfilling. Two tablespoons per wrapper — stuffed rolls split and leak.
  4. Skipping the flip. The basket side stays pale; one turn at halfway keeps it even.
  5. Skipping the oil spray. Wrappers carry no fat; a thin coat is what turns them gold.

Frequently asked questions

How long do frozen egg rolls take in an air fryer? 12–15 minutes at 380°F / 193°C, flipped at halfway. Mini rolls need 9–12 minutes. No thawing and no oil needed.

Do egg rolls need oil in the air fryer? Frozen ones carry their own coating. Homemade wrapped rolls need a light spray — the wrapper itself has no fat and browns patchy without it.

Why are my egg rolls soggy? Hot filling, overfilling or a skipped flip. Cool the filling completely, use two tablespoons per wrapper, and turn once at halfway.

Can I cook raw-meat fillings inside a wrapped roll? No — the short cook browns the wrapper but cannot safely cook raw meat inside. Cook the filling fully first: 160°F / 71°C for pork, 165°F / 74°C for poultry.

Can I freeze homemade egg rolls? Yes — freeze them unwrapped on a tray until solid, then bag them. They cook from frozen at 12–15 minutes and keep for months.

Egg rolls reward the same three habits every time: cold filling, light spray, one flip at halfway. The air fryer does the rest — crisp wrappers with none of the deep-fryer mess.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Falafel: Time and Temperature for Crisp Centers
entry.summary: Air fryer falafel times for fresh-mix and frozen patties, with 380°F / 193°C settings, the flip rule and fixes for dry or falling-apart falafel.
entry.content:
Falafel might be the dish the air fryer improves most: deep-fried falafel soaks oil and turns heavy, while air-fried falafel crisps on the outside and stays tender inside with a fraction of the fat. The two failure modes are dry falafel and falafel that falls apart — and both are fixed in the mix, not the basket.

This chart covers fresh-mix and frozen falafel, the flip rule and the fixes.

Times vary by appliance model. Patty size, mix moisture and basket crowding change the clock — watch the first batch and adjust.

Air fryer falafel chart

Falafel is ground chickpeas and herbs — there is no raw-meat timing, so doneness is texture and color: deep gold with crisp edges and a tender center.

FalafelTemperatureTimeNotes
Fresh mix, 1.5-inch patties380°F / 193°C12–15 minFlip at halfway
Frozen patties380°F / 193°C12–15 minNo thawing, flip once
Small balls, 1 inch380°F / 193°C10–12 minShake once
Pita-crisp finish400°F / 205°C2–3 minLast minutes only
Oil-sprayed patties380°F / 193°C12–15 minEven browning, light spray

Start checking at the low end. Falafel holds well past done — a minute or two extra costs little, which makes it one of the most forgiving items in the basket.

The mix: where dry and crumbly are fixed

Two ingredients decide whether falafel holds together: soaked dried chickpeas (never canned) and enough binding moisture.

ProblemCauseThe fix
Falls apartCanned chickpeas — too soft and wetSoak dried chickpeas overnight, grind raw
Falls apartToo little binderAdd 1–2 tbsp flour or breadcrumbs per cup of mix
Dry interiorMix ground too fine or cooked too longCoarse grind, pull at golden
Dry exteriorNo oilA light spray before cooking

The classic method is non-negotiable: dried chickpeas soaked overnight (12+ hours), ground raw with parsley, cilantro, onion, garlic and cumin. Canned chickpeas are pre-cooked — their starch is gone, and the mix falls apart no matter what the basket does.

Rest the shaped patties 15 minutes in the refrigerator before cooking — the mix firms and holds its shape in the basket.

Serving: the pita build

Warm the pitas in the basket after the falafel comes out — 350°F / 177°C for 2 minutes per side. Build with tahini sauce, chopped tomatoes and pickles; the tahini thins with a spoon of water to a pourable sauce.

StepTimeNotes
Falafel, per the chart12–15 minDeep gold, crisp edges
Pitas in the basket350°F / 177°C, 2 min/sideWarm and pliable
Tahini sauce—Thin with water to pourable

Everything lands hot at once — falafel, warm pita, cold vegetables — the contrast that makes the sandwich work.

Five mistakes with air fryer falafel

  1. Canned chickpeas. Their starch is gone; the mix falls apart. Soak dried chickpeas overnight.
  2. Cooking right after shaping. Rest the patties 15 minutes refrigerated so they firm.
  3. Skipping the oil spray. A dry surface stays pale and chalky; a light spray browns evenly.
  4. Overcrowding. Patties touching steam each other; one layer with air between.
  5. Grinding to a paste. Coarse grind holds texture; a fine paste turns dense and dry.

Frequently asked questions

How long does falafel take in an air fryer? 12–15 minutes at 380°F / 193°C for 1.5-inch patties, flipped at halfway. Small balls need 10–12 minutes; frozen patties cook from frozen at the same time.

Do I need to thaw frozen falafel? No — straight into the basket at the same time and temperature as fresh.

Why does my falafel fall apart? The mix: canned chickpeas or too little binder. Soak dried chickpeas overnight and grind them raw, with 1–2 tablespoons of flour or breadcrumbs per cup.

Why is my falafel dry? A fine grind or too long a cook. Grind coarse, pull at deep gold, and spray lightly with oil before cooking.

Can I cook falafel from a boxed mix? Yes — follow the box's hydration, rest the shaped patties 15 minutes, then 12–15 minutes at 380°F / 193°C.

Falafel rewards the mix: overnight-soaked chickpeas, coarse grind, a rest before cooking. The air fryer handles the rest — crisp outside, tender inside, without the deep-fryer oil.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Fish: Times and Temperatures for Cod, Tilapia, Haddock and Catfish
entry.summary: Air fryer fish times by thickness for cod, tilapia, haddock and catfish, plus frozen breaded fillets, the 145°F / 63°C rule and why fillets fall apart.
entry.content:
Fish is the best value in an air fryer: a fillet goes from cold to plated in under fifteen minutes, with a crisp edge instead of a soggy pan. It is also the protein most likely to come out in pieces.

Two things decide whether you get a whole fillet. Thickness, not weight, sets the clock. And the basket floor decides whether the fillet survives the flip.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. Wattage and basket size change the clock, but 145°F / 63°C does not change.

The rule: 145°F / 63°C for fish

FishSafe internal temperature
Cod, tilapia, haddock, catfish, all white fish145°F / 63°C
Salmon, tuna and other oily fish145°F / 63°C
Frozen breaded fish, cooked from frozen165°F / 74°C
Reheated fish leftovers165°F / 74°C

Fish carry no rest-time allowance and no ground-meat exception. The one number that surprises people is frozen breaded fish: the package product is a prepared food, so reheating it puts it under the 165°F / 74°C reheating standard rather than the fresh-fish number.

Probe the thickest part of the fillet, entering from the side rather than the top, because a thin fillet is shorter than the probe's sensing tip. If the reading looks low, move the probe and read again before you add time.

Air fryer fish chart by thickness

Thickness is the only measurement that matters here. Two fillets can both weigh six ounces while one is half an inch thick and the other is nearly two inches. The thick one needs several more minutes, and the thin one is done before you expect it.

Fish and thicknessTemperatureTimeNotes
Cod, 0.5 inch400°F / 205°C7–9 minCheck at 6 min
Cod, 1 inch400°F / 205°C10–14 minThick flakes, mild
Cod, 1.5 inches380°F / 193°C14–18 minLower heat, longer time
Tilapia, 0.5 inch390°F / 199°C6–8 minVery thin edges
Tilapia, 1 inch390°F / 199°C9–12 minDelicate, flip with care
Haddock, 1 inch390°F / 199°C10–13 minSlightly denser than cod
Haddock, 1.5 inches380°F / 193°C14–17 minCheck at 12 min
Catfish, 1 inch400°F / 205°C10–14 minFirm flesh, holds up well
Catfish nuggets, 1 inch pieces400°F / 205°C8–11 minShake at 5 min
Any white fish, 2 inches370°F / 188°C18–22 minRare, check at 16 min

A general shortcut: one inch of fillet needs roughly ten minutes at 390–400°F / 199–205°C. Every additional half inch of thickness adds about three to four minutes, and the temperature should drop slightly as the fillet gets thicker.

Frozen breaded fillets and fish sticks

Frozen breaded fish is the easiest fish to cook, because the coating is engineered to crisp and the product is usually par-cooked before freezing. It goes in from frozen, in a single layer, with no oil added.

Frozen breaded fishTemperatureTimeNotes
Fish sticks400°F / 205°C8–10 minShake at 5 min
Breaded fillets, thin400°F / 205°C10–12 minFlip at halfway
Breaded fillets, thick390°F / 199°C12–15 minSingle layer, no stack
Beer-battered fillets400°F / 205°C10–13 minBatter drips, use a liner
Panko-crusted fillets390°F / 199°C11–14 minPanko browns fast

Never stack frozen breaded fish. Two layers means the coating on the bottom fillets stays pale and steams while the top layer burns, and the pieces fuse together as they thaw.

Why fish falls apart in the basket

Fish muscle is built in short flakes held together by thin connective sheets. Heat makes those sheets contract, and the flakes separate. Add a wet surface and a sticky basket and the fillet tears the moment you try to lift it. Four habits prevent it:

  1. Dry the fillet, then oil the fish and the basket. A dry surface browns and releases; a wet one glues itself down.
  2. Preheat for three minutes. A hot basket sets the bottom surface before the fillet can stick.
  3. Use a slotted spatula, not tongs. Tongs pinch a flaky fillet in half. Slide the spatula under and lift straight up.
  4. Flip once at most. Every extra touch is a chance to lose a corner.

If the fillet is very thin, lay it on a small piece of perforated parchment and lift the parchment out at the end. Do not use a solid sheet, and never let parchment touch the heating element.

Uneven fillets are the other failure. Fold the thin tail under the fillet so the whole piece is one thickness, and it will cook evenly instead of drying at one end while the other end finishes.

Five mistakes with air fryer fish

  1. Cooking by the clock. A thin fillet goes from done to dry in about 90 seconds.
  2. A wet fillet. Surface water steams the fish and stops browning.
  3. Using weight instead of thickness. A thick six-ounce fillet and a thin six-ounce fillet need different times.
  4. Cranking the heat on a thick fillet. Above 400°F / 205°C the outside sets before the center is done.
  5. Adding oil to a breaded fillet. The coating already crisps, and oil makes it soft.

Frequently asked questions

How long does fish take in an air fryer?

One inch of fresh white fish takes 9–14 minutes at 390–400°F / 199–205°C, depending on the species. Breaded frozen fillets take 10–15 minutes at 390–400°F / 199–205°C. Probe the thickest part and pull the fish at 145°F / 63°C.

Can I cook frozen fish fillets without thawing?

Yes, for breaded or par-cooked products, which are formulated to cook from frozen. Raw frozen fillets are harder to verify and cook unevenly at the edges. Thaw them in the refrigerator overnight, then use the fresh chart.

Should I flip fish in the air fryer?

A fillet an inch thick or less usually needs no flip. Thicker fillets benefit from one gentle turn at the halfway point, using a slotted spatula rather than tongs.

How do I know when fish is done without a thermometer?

You do not, reliably. Fish turns opaque, flakes separate when pressed, and the center loses its glassy look, but those are guesses that arrive late. A thermometer reading 145°F / 63°C is a measurement.

Is catfish different from other white fish?

It is firmer and holds together better, so it survives a flip more easily. Use the same temperature and add a minute or two over cod of the same thickness.

The short version

Pat the fillet dry, oil it lightly, preheat the basket, and cook in a single layer at 390–400°F / 199–205°C for 7–14 minutes according to thickness. Lift it with a slotted spatula, turn it once at most, and pull it at 145°F / 63°C.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Frozen Foods Chart (Times and Temperatures)
entry.summary: Printable air fryer times and temperatures for frozen fries, nuggets, wings and pizza, plus the safe internal temperatures worth checking.
entry.content:
Frozen food is the reason most people keep an air fryer on the counter. No thawing, no oil, no waiting for a big oven to heat up — fries come out crisp in the time a microwave would make them soggy.

The catch is that your machine is not my machine. Basket size, wattage and how close the element sits to the food all shift the clock by a few minutes. So every number below is a range, and every range assumes a single layer in a preheated basket.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer, not the clock, as your final check.

The rule that beats every time on this chart

A time range tells you when to start looking. It never tells you whether food is safe. Only an instant-read thermometer does that, and it should go into the thickest part, away from bone and fat.

Frozen foodSafe internal temperature
Breaded chicken nuggets, wings, tenders165°F / 74°C
Breaded fish fillets, fish sticks145°F / 63°C
Frozen meatballs (beef or pork)160°F / 71°C
Frozen meatballs (chicken or turkey)165°F / 74°C
Frozen shrimp, cooked from frozen145°F / 63°C
Frozen vegetablesNo minimum — cook to texture
Reheated leftovers of any kind165°F / 74°C

Frozen pizza and frozen vegetables are the two categories where texture, not safety, is the target. Everything breaded around meat or fish needs the thermometer.

Air fryer frozen foods chart

Frozen foodTemperatureTimeNotes
French fries, shoestring400°F / 205°C12–15 minShake at halfway
French fries, steak cut400°F / 205°C18–22 minShake twice
French fries, waffle400°F / 205°C12–16 minDo not stack
Tater tots400°F / 205°C14–18 minShake twice
Chicken nuggets400°F / 205°C10–12 minSingle layer only
Chicken wings380°F / 193°C22–26 minShake every 8 min
Mozzarella sticks390°F / 199°C7–9 minWatch the last 2 min
Onion rings390°F / 199°C8–10 minShake once
Fish fillets, breaded400°F / 205°C10–12 minFlip at halfway
Fish sticks400°F / 205°C8–10 minShake once
Personal pizza380°F / 193°C6–9 minCheck at 6 min
Frozen shrimp, raw peeled390°F / 199°C6–8 minDone when pink
Frozen meatballs390°F / 199°C10–12 minShake at 6 min
Frozen vegetables390°F / 199°C10–14 minShake at halfway

Pizza and cheese sticks are the two items that go from right to ruined in under a minute. Stand next to the machine for those.

Frozen fries: three shapes, three timings

Shoestring fries are thin, so they crisp fast and dry out fast. Waffle fries have more surface area and hold heat unevenly, which is why they sit between shoestring and steak cut. Steak-cut fries are thick enough that the inside needs real time — if you pull them at 12 minutes you get a hot, raw center.

For all three: preheat first, spread them in one layer, and shake the basket at least once. A pile of fries steams. Steamed fries are pale and limp no matter how long you leave them.

Frozen chicken and fish: the thermometer foods

Breaded frozen chicken is the category where people guess most and get it wrong most. Nuggets and tenders look done — golden, crisp, hot — at internal temperatures well below 165°F / 74°C. Color is not a safety signal, and breading insulates the meat, so the outside always finishes first.

Push the probe in from the side of a nugget or the thickest end of a tender. If it reads under 165°F / 74°C, give it 2–3 more minutes and check again. Frozen fish fillets and fish sticks need 145°F / 63°C, and they overcook quickly once they pass it, so check early.

Five mistakes with frozen food

  1. Skipping the preheat. Frozen food drops basket temperature hard. Three minutes of preheat keeps the outside crisp.
  2. Overcrowding. Two layers means the middle layer steams. Cook in batches instead.
  3. Not shaking. Anything in a pile needs a shake every 8–10 minutes.
  4. Adding oil to breaded items. They are already coated. Oil makes the breading soggy.
  5. Trusting the package time. Package directions assume a different machine. Start at the low end and add minutes.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to thaw frozen food before air frying? No for fries, nuggets, wings, mozzarella sticks, onion rings, fish, shrimp and vegetables — those are formulated to cook from frozen. Meatballs and anything you formed yourself should be thawed so the center cooks before the outside burns.

Why are my frozen fries still soft in the middle? Almost always overcrowding or a cold basket. Cook fewer at a time, preheat, and shake twice. Very thick steak-cut fries may also need 20–22 minutes rather than 18.

Can I stack mozzarella sticks? No. The coating needs direct hot air on all sides. Stacked sticks fuse into one mass and the cheese escapes.

Is a frozen personal pizza better in the air fryer or the oven? The air fryer, if the pizza fits flat with a little space around it. The crust crisps underneath in a way a baking sheet rarely manages.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Grilled Cheese: Time, Temperature and Crisp Rules
entry.summary: How to make grilled cheese in an air fryer, with 370°F / 188°C times for different breads, the flip rule and fixes for soggy or burnt results.
entry.content:
Grilled cheese is the fastest way to learn your air fryer's personality. There is no thermometer to check and no safe temperature to hit — just bread, butter and cheese, and a machine that browns the outside far faster than a skillet ever could.

The challenge is the opposite of every meat recipe: instead of worrying about the center, you are managing the surface. The air fryer will happily turn butter into gold and then into char in about two minutes, so the times below are about watching, not walking away.

Times vary by appliance model. Bread thickness, cheese moisture and butter coverage change the clock — there is no internal temperature target for this one.

Air fryer grilled cheese chart

Assemble the sandwich with butter on the outside of both slices, then toast at a moderate temperature so the cheese melts before the bread darkens.

SandwichTemperatureTimeNotes
Standard white or sourdough370°F / 188°C8–10 minFlip at 4–5 min
Thick-cut artisan bread370°F / 188°C10–12 minFlip once, press lightly
Thin sandwich bread350°F / 177°C6–8 minWatch closely, flip halfway
Extra cheese, double decker350°F / 177°C10–12 minLonger melt, lower heat
Open-faced melt370°F / 188°C6–8 minNo flip, cheese on top

The flip is what separates even toasting from one golden side and one pale one. Use a spatula and flip confidently — melted cheese pulls, but a quick turn keeps the sandwich together.

Why 370°F / 188°C is the sweet spot

Cheese melts fully between 150°F / 66°C and 180°F / 82°C, but it needs time. Bread browns quickly in moving hot air. A moderate temperature gives the cheese time to become pourable while the butter on the outside crisps gradually.

TemperatureWhat happens
320°F / 160°CCheese melts well, bread toasts slowly and evenly
350°F / 177°CGood balance for thick bread or heavy cheese
370°F / 188°CThe all-rounder: crisp outside, fully melted middle
400°F / 205°CFast, but the outside can char before the middle melts

If your first sandwich comes out dark on the outside and stiff in the middle, drop 20 degrees and add two minutes. The bread you use shifts the balance more than anything else — dense sourdough absorbs time, thin white bread burns in it.

The butter question

Butter on the outside is the classic for a reason: it browns evenly and carries flavor into the crust. Two alternatives work in the air fryer:

  • Mayonnaise on the outside browns slightly faster and more evenly — a useful trick for breads that scorch.
  • Brushing the bread with oil works but browns patchy; butter and mayo coat more uniformly.

Butter the bread, not the basket. Butter in the basket smokes, spatters and makes cleanup miserable for no benefit — the sandwich carries its own fat.

Fillings that behave and fillings that fight

The air fryer heats fillings with the same air that toasts the bread, so choose accordingly:

  • Slices of cheese melt evenly; shredded cheese melts faster but can slide out when flipped.
  • Thin tomato slices add moisture that softens the bread — pat them dry first.
  • Deli meats warm through in the same time; no adjustment needed.
  • Thick or cold fillings (chili, pulled meat) insulate the middle — lower the temperature and extend the time so the heat reaches the center.

Two slices of cheese is the reliability limit. Beyond that, the outer bread browns before the stack melts, and the fix is always lower-and-longer, not hotter.

Five mistakes with air fryer grilled cheese

  1. Starting at 400°F / 205°C. The crust wins the race and the cheese stays firm in the middle.
  2. Skipping the flip. One-sided toasting is the most common complaint and the easiest fix.
  3. Buttering the basket instead of the bread. All smoke, no crunch.
  4. Piling on four slices of cheese. The stack insulates; lower the heat or accept unmelted pockets.
  5. Walking away. The difference between golden and burnt is two minutes in moving air.

Frequently asked questions

What temperature do you grill cheese in an air fryer? 370°F / 188°C for standard bread, 8–10 minutes with a flip halfway. Use 350°F / 177°C for thick bread, extra cheese or delicate fillings.

How do you keep the sandwich from flying around? Lighter baskets can lift thin sandwiches. A metal toast rack or two toothpicks through the top corners holds it down — remove them before cutting.

Do you need to preheat for grilled cheese? Two or three minutes helps the first sandwich brown evenly. It is less critical than for meat, since there is no safety timing involved.

Why is my bread burnt but the cheese cold? The temperature was too high or the fillings too thick. Drop to 350°F / 177°C, extend the time, and let cheese slices sit at room temperature for ten minutes before assembling.

Can you reheat a grilled cheese in the air fryer? Yes — 350°F / 177°C for 3–4 minutes brings back most of the crunch. Add a minute for thick or double-decker sandwiches.

Grilled cheese teaches the core air fryer skill: controlling surface browning with temperature and time. Master the flip and the 370°F / 188°C sweet spot, and every melt, toast and quesadilla that follows will behave.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Hamburgers: Juicy Patties at the Right Temperature
entry.summary: Air fryer hamburger times for fresh and frozen patties, with 380°F / 193°C settings, flip timing and the 160°F / 71°C ground beef rule.
entry.content:
The air fryer cooks burgers with the same hot air that crisps fries, so the outside browns and the fat that renders stays with the patty instead of dripping onto coals. It is faster than a grill to heat up and less messy than a skillet — but ground beef has a fixed safety rule, and a burger is the one shape where undercooking is easy to miss.

The chart below covers fresh and frozen patties. Under USDA rules, ground beef must reach 160°F / 71°C inside — there is no thickness, cheese or bun that changes that number.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. Wattage, basket size and patty thickness change the clock, but 160°F / 71°C does not change.

The rule for ground beef

Whole steaks can be safely cooked to lower temperatures because bacteria live on the surface. Ground beef mixes the surface into the center, so the center must be cooked too:

Ground beefSafe internal temperature
Fresh patties, any thickness160°F / 71°C
Frozen patties, cooked from frozen160°F / 71°C
Burgers reheated later160°F / 71°C

Probe the center of the patty from the side, horizontally, so the thermometer tip sits in the middle of the meat. A vertical probe can push the tip through the thin bottom and read the hot basket air instead.

Air fryer hamburger chart: fresh patties

Times assume a preheated basket, patties of even thickness and a single layer. Dimple the center of each patty with your thumb — it keeps the middle from bulging.

PattyTemperatureTimeNotes
Fresh, 1/4 lb, 1/2 inch thick380°F / 193°C8–10 minFlip at halfway
Fresh, 1/3 lb, 3/4 inch thick380°F / 193°C10–12 minFlip at halfway
Fresh, 1/2 lb, 1 inch thick380°F / 193°C12–15 minFlip once, check early
Stuffed or filled patty380°F / 193°C12–15 minVerify the center carefully
Smashed-style thin patties380°F / 193°C6–8 minVery thin; probe carefully

Cheese goes on in the last minute, after the patty has reached temperature. The residual heat and 30 seconds in the warm basket melt it without extending the cook.

Air fryer hamburger chart: frozen patties

Frozen patties are pre-formed and often pre-seasoned, and they cook evenly from frozen. No thawing and no pressing — pressing squeezes moisture out.

Frozen pattyTemperatureTimeNotes
1/4 lb frozen patty380°F / 193°C12–15 minFlip at halfway
1/3 lb frozen patty380°F / 193°C14–17 minFlip at halfway
1/2 lb frozen patty380°F / 193°C16–19 minCheck at 14 minutes
Thin frozen patties380°F / 193°C10–12 minShake or flip once

Frozen patties frequently need the long end of their range. The center thaws as it cooks, so the thermometer should confirm the middle before you build the burger.

Fat, smoke and the drip tray

Burgers release fat as they cook, and in an air fryer that fat collects under the basket. Two habits keep the smoke down: cook within the chart's temperatures rather than hotter, and empty or wipe the drawer between batches. Adding water to the drip tray — a tablespoon under the basket — also catches spatter and reduces smoke on fatty blends.

An 80/20 blend gives the juiciest result. Leaner beef dries out faster than the chart's shortest time; fattier blends splatter more. Either way, the internal temperature target does not move.

Five mistakes with air fryer burgers

  1. Judging by the crust. A deep-brown outside can hide a raw center; probe the middle every time.
  2. Pressing patties during cooking. Pressing squeezes out the juices that make burgers tender.
  3. Cooking straight from the fridge. Cold centers lag; let patties sit out 15 minutes for even timing.
  4. Overworking the meat. Compact patties turn dense; mix just until the seasoning is spread.
  5. Skipping the dimple. Flat-center patties dome up and cook unevenly at the edges.

Frequently asked questions

How long do burgers take in an air fryer? 8–12 minutes at 380°F / 193°C for fresh quarter- to third-pound patties, flipped halfway; frozen patties need 12–17 minutes. Verify the center reaches 160°F / 71°C.

What temperature do air fryer burgers need inside? 160°F / 71°C — the USDA minimum for all ground beef, fresh or frozen. Use an instant-read thermometer through the side of the patty.

Can I cook a medium-rare burger? Ground beef must reach 160°F / 71°C under USDA rules, which rules out rare and medium-rare. A steak can be cooked lower because its center never touched the surface; ground beef has no such exception.

Do burgers smoke in an air fryer? Some smoke is normal with fatty beef. Keep the temperature at or below 380°F / 193°C, wipe the drawer between batches, and add a spoon of water to the drip tray.

Can I cook burgers and fries together? Not well. Fries need shaking and dry air; burgers release fat. Cook the burgers first, wipe the drawer, then cook fries at 400°F / 205°C.

Burgers in the air fryer are simple once you accept the thermometer. Even patties with a dimple, 380°F / 193°C, a flip at halfway, and 160°F / 71°C in the middle — everything else is garnish.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Hard Boiled Eggs (Times by Doneness)
entry.summary: Air fryer hard boiled eggs by doneness, with soft, jammy and hard times, hot start and cold start methods, the ice bath and honest peeling notes.
entry.content:
Air frying eggs is not frying, and it is not boiling. You set whole eggs in the shell in the basket, run the machine low, and take them out with no pot to scrub.

The results are real, and so are the limits. Here are the times by doneness, plus an honest answer on peeling.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer for meat and a timer for eggs. Wattage and basket size move the clock more for eggs than for anything else.

Why people cook eggs in an air fryer

Two reasons: hands-off cooking with no pot of water to heat, and the claim that air fryer eggs peel more easily, which this page deals with below.

The trade is that a shell hides everything: you cannot see the yolk set, and you cannot read the center of an intact egg without breaking it. Time is your only control.

Air fryer egg chart by doneness

Times are for large eggs from the refrigerator, in a single layer, in a basket that was not preheated.

DonenessTemperatureTimeYolk and white
Soft250°F / 121°C8–11 minRunny yolk, white barely set
Soft-medium250°F / 121°C11–13 minThick liquid yolk, set white
Jammy250°F / 121°C13–16 minFudgy, glossy yolk, no run
Hard250°F / 121°C16–19 minFully set yolk, firm white
Very firm260°F / 127°C18–21 minDry, pale yolk that slices

Medium eggs finish 1–2 minutes early and extra-large eggs need 1–2 minutes more. If the shells keep cracking, drop to 240°F / 116°C.

Hot start versus cold start

A cold start puts the eggs in a room-temperature basket and then starts the machine. A hot start preheats for about 3 minutes first. Both work; the choice is about time and cracking.

MethodTemperatureJammyHardWhat changes
Cold start250°F / 121°C13–16 min16–19 minGentler on the shell, more forgiving
Hot start250°F / 121°C11–13 min14–16 minFaster, but shells crack more often

Never stack eggs in two layers, and turn them once at halfway.

Ice bath, then peel

Move the eggs straight from the basket into ice water for 5–10 minutes. The cooking stops instead of coasting, which keeps a jammy yolk jammy, and the egg pulls away from the shell membrane as it cools.

To peel, tap the wide end on the counter until the shell cracks — that is where the air pocket sits. Roll the egg under your palm to craze the shell, then peel from the wide end in a bowl of cold water.

The peeling debate: what is actually proven

Search this topic and you will find confident claims that air fryer eggs peel perfectly every time. Treat them as anecdotal; no controlled comparison against boiled eggs has been published.

What is known about peeling has little to do with the heat source. Very fresh eggs are harder to peel, because the white holds more carbon dioxide and the membrane clings. You will still get a torn egg now and then, so a chart that promises a perfect peel every time is describing luck.

What the air fryer does not do better than boiling

Boiling is not a worse method, just a different one, and in several ways it is the better tool:

  • Volume. A basket holds 6–8 large eggs in one layer. A pot holds 12 or more.
  • Evenness. Water surrounds each egg at one temperature. Moving air does not, so doneness varies.
  • Repeatability. Boiling has a timeline you learn once. Air fryer timing shifts with wattage and basket size.

The air fryer wins the small batch: 2–6 eggs, no stove, no waiting for a boil.

Egg safety, plainly

USDA lists 160°F / 71°C for egg dishes — custards, quiches, casseroles — and 145°F / 63°C for shell eggs cooked to order for immediate service. Neither is a probe-and-pull instruction for a whole egg, because there is no practical way to read the middle of an intact shell.

So use time and one test egg: crack the smallest first, and add 2 minutes if it is looser than you wanted. Refrigerate what you do not eat within two hours.

Five mistakes with air fryer eggs

  1. Stacking eggs. Two layers means the top eggs cook faster and the bottom ones stay raw.
  2. Skipping the ice bath. Carryover heat keeps cooking the yolk after the basket stops.
  3. Using the hottest setting. The white turns rubbery before the yolk is ready.
  4. Peeling immediately. Give the eggs 5–10 minutes in ice water first, or the white tears.
  5. Judging by the shell. A cracked shell says nothing about the yolk inside.

Frequently asked questions

How long do hard boiled eggs take in an air fryer? 16–19 minutes at 250°F / 121°C from a cold start for large eggs. Check one egg at 16 minutes and add time in 2-minute steps.

Do air fryer eggs really peel easier? Some people report it, but it is anecdotal rather than measured. Egg age, an ice bath and peeling from the wide end matter more than the appliance.

Why is there a green ring around my yolk? That is iron and sulfur from the white reacting at the yolk surface, which means the egg was cooked long or cooled slowly. Pull the eggs 1 minute earlier and use the ice bath.

The short version

Air fryer eggs are a small-batch tool, not a replacement for a pot. Use 250°F / 121°C, give them 8–19 minutes for the yolk you want, turn them once, and ice-bath them the moment they come out.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Hot Dogs: Time and Temperature for Perfect Franks
entry.summary: Air fryer hot dog times for whole, split and toasted buns, with 390°F / 199°C settings and the heating rule for ready-to-eat franks.
entry.content:
Hot dogs are the fastest food in the air fryer — dinner in under ten minutes with a snappier casing than boiling ever gives. They are also the food people overthink: franks are ready-to-eat, so the job is heating and browning, not cooking raw meat.

This chart covers whole dogs, split dogs and toasting the buns in the same basket.

Times vary by appliance model. Franks are fully cooked — heat them until steaming hot throughout, 165°F / 74°C at the center is the safe target.

Air fryer hot dog chart

Franks need no oil, no piercing and no prep. The casing browns in moving air; piercing drains the juices that keep the dog snappy.

Hot dogTemperatureTimeNotes
Whole franks390°F / 199°C4–6 minRoll once at halfway
Split lengthwise390°F / 199°C3–5 minCut side up, charred edges
From the refrigerator, cold390°F / 199°C5–7 minLonger than room temperature
Buns, split open350°F / 177°C2–3 minAfter the dogs, butter optional
Chili cheese dogs, assembled390°F / 199°C3–4 minMelt only, watch closely

The visual cue is done before you think: the casing browns and blisters quickly. A frank heats through in 4 minutes at 390°F / 199°C; anything past 7 minutes toughens the casing.

Why the air fryer beats boiling

Boiling waterlogs the casing and washes out the cure's flavor. The air fryer keeps the frank dry, browns the casing and concentrates the flavor — the same reason bacon cooks well in one.

MethodTimeResult
Boiling5–7 minPale, waterlogged, snappy but bland
Air fryer, whole4–6 minBrowned casing, concentrated flavor
Air fryer, split3–5 minCharred edges, fastest

For the classic diner treatment, split the dogs lengthwise (not through), lay them cut side up, and let the edges char. The flat surfaces hold toppings better too.

Buns in the same basket

Toasting buns after the dogs come out is the two-minute upgrade that matters: split them open, lay them cut side up, 350°F / 177°C for 2–3 minutes. Butter the cut side first for griddle-style toast.

Timing the whole meal: dogs first (4–6 minutes), buns second (2–3 minutes), assemble immediately. Everything lands hot at once without juggling a stovetop.

Five mistakes with air fryer hot dogs

  1. Piercing the casing. Every hole drains the snap; tongs and a roll at halfway instead.
  2. Cooking past 7 minutes. The casing toughens and splits; 4–6 minutes at 390°F / 199°C is the window.
  3. Skipping the bun toast. Two minutes at 350°F / 177°C is the upgrade people notice most.
  4. Cold franks straight in. Add a minute or two, or rest them 10 minutes first for even heating.
  5. Assembling chili dogs too early. The bun steams; assemble just before the short melt.

Frequently asked questions

How long do hot dogs take in an air fryer? 4–6 minutes at 390°F / 199°C for whole franks, rolled once. Split dogs take 3–5 minutes; cold franks from the refrigerator need 5–7.

Do hot dogs need oil in the air fryer? No. The casing browns on its own in moving hot air, and piercing drains the juices anyway.

What temperature heats hot dogs safely? Franks are ready-to-eat — heat until steaming hot throughout; 165°F / 74°C at the center is the safe target for reheated and ready-to-eat meats.

Can I cook hot dogs and buns together? The timing differs — dogs first, then buns for the last 2–3 minutes at 350°F / 177°C. Cooking both from the start overcooks the dogs.

Why did my hot dogs split? Too long or too hot. Keep them at 390°F / 199°C for 4–6 minutes and roll once — split casing means overcooked.

Hot dogs reward simplicity: no prep, 390°F / 199°C, 4–6 minutes, buns toasted after. The air fryer makes them better than boiling with zero cleanup.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Lamb Chops: Time and Temperature by Thickness
entry.summary: Air fryer lamb chop times by thickness, with 400°F / 205°C settings, the 145°F / 63°C internal rule, carryover cooking and the rest.
entry.content:
Lamb chops are the fastest premium cut in the air fryer: rib or loin chops cook in ten to fourteen minutes with a browned crust and a rosy center. They are also expensive enough that every minute past done costs real money — the thermometer decides.

This chart covers chops by thickness, the temperatures and the rest that keeps them tender.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. Thickness and starting temperature change the clock, but 145°F / 63°C plus rest does not change.

The rule for lamb chops

Lamb chops are whole cuts, so the simple USDA standard applies:

CutSafe internal temperatureRest
Lamb rib or loin chops145°F / 63°C3 minutes
Lamb leg, whole145°F / 63°C3 minutes
Ground lamb (not chops)160°F / 71°CNone

Probe the thickest part of the chop, away from the bone. The bone in a rib chop reads high; angle the thermometer into the muscle.

Air fryer lamb chops chart

Times assume a preheated basket and chops that start near room temperature — out of the refrigerator 20–30 minutes before cooking. A cold chop lags at the center while the crust hardens.

ChopTemperatureTimeNotes
Rib chops, 1 inch400°F / 205°C10–12 minFlip at halfway
Loin chops, 1 inch400°F / 205°C10–12 minFlip at halfway
Thick chops, 1.5 inch400°F / 205°C12–15 minCheck at 11 min
Thin chops, 3/4 inch400°F / 205°C8–10 minWatch closely
Charred finish425°F / 218°C1–2 minOptional, last minutes

Start checking at the low end. A chop climbs from 145°F / 63°C to well-done in only a few minutes — and those minutes are the difference between rosy and gray.

The rest and the carryover

The USDA's 145°F / 63°C standard includes a three minute rest, and the chop keeps cooking after it leaves the basket:

Pull from basketAfter a 5-minute restResult
145°F / 63°CAbout 150°F / 66°CRosy pink center, juicy
150°F / 66°CAbout 155°F / 68°CBarely pink, firm
155°F / 68°CAbout 160°F / 71°CWell-done, drier

All three are safe — 145°F / 63°C with rest is the floor, and anything above it is texture. Rest the chops 5 minutes under loose foil, then serve.

Seasoning that suits lamb

Lamb carries strong flavors well: garlic, rosemary, oregano, cumin and salt — a dry rub that goes on before cooking. Mint chutney and chimichurri arrive after the heat. A thin coat of oil helps the crust; lamb fat renders enough on its own for most chops.

Five mistakes with air fryer lamb chops

  1. Cooking from the refrigerator. A cold center lags; rest the chops 20–30 minutes first.
  2. Cooking past 145°F / 63°C in the basket. The rest finishes the job more gently than extra heat.
  3. Probing against the bone. Rib chops read high at the bone; angle into the muscle.
  4. Overcooking thin chops. 3/4-inch chops finish in 8–10 minutes; two extra minutes grays them.
  5. Crowding the basket. Chops touching steam each other; one layer with air between.

Frequently asked questions

How long do lamb chops take in an air fryer? 10–12 minutes at 400°F / 205°C for 1-inch rib or loin chops, flipped halfway. Thick chops need 12–15 minutes; thin ones 8–10.

What temperature should lamb chops be inside? 145°F / 63°C in the thickest part, followed by a three minute rest, per USDA rules for whole cuts of lamb. The center stays rosy pink — that is correct and safe.

Is pink lamb safe? At 145°F / 63°C with a proper rest, yes — USDA guidance for whole cuts says exactly that. Ground lamb is the exception: it must reach 160°F / 71°C.

Why are my lamb chops tough? They cooked past temperature or skipped the rest. Pull at 145°F / 63°C, rest five minutes, and slice against the grain.

Do lamb chops need oil? A thin coat helps the crust form evenly; fattier chops render enough on their own.

Lamb chops reward precision: room-temperature start, 400°F / 205°C, pulled at 145°F / 63°C, rested five minutes. Ten minutes later the fastest premium cut in the air fryer is done.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Lobster Tail: Time and Temperature by Size
entry.summary: Air fryer lobster tail times by ounce, with the butterfly cut, 380°F / 193°C settings and the 145°F / 63°C internal temperature rule.
entry.content:
Lobster tail is the fastest luxury in the air fryer: a butterflied tail cooks in under ten minutes with butter-basted meat that beats boiling on every count. Boiling waters out the flavor; the air fryer concentrates it.

The one rule that matters: the butterfly cut and the internal temperature of the meat.

Times vary by appliance model — use a thermometer. Tail size changes the clock, but 145°F / 63°C does not change.

The rule for lobster

Lobster is shellfish, and shellfish cooks to the same standard as fish under FDA guidance:

LobsterSafe internal temperature
Butterfly tail, any size145°F / 63°C
Whole lobster, boiled or steamed145°F / 63°C
Lobster meat reheated145°F / 63°C

Probe the thickest part of the tail meat. Overcooked lobster turns rubbery fast — pull at temperature, not past it.

The butterfly cut

Butterflying the tail is what makes the air fryer version work: kitchen shears cut down the top of the shell to the tail fan, the shell opens, and the meat lifts above the shell — exposed to the hot air on every side.

StepTimeWhy
Shears down the top of the shell1 minExposes the meat to the air
Loosen the meat, lift it onto the shell1 minEven cooking on all sides
Butter, paprika and salt over the meat—Bastes as it cooks

A tail cooked inside an uncut shell steams unevenly — the exposed meat is what the air fryer needs.

Air fryer lobster tail chart

Times assume a preheated basket and butterflied tails of similar size.

Tail sizeTemperatureTimeNotes
4 oz380°F / 193°C6–8 minVerify at 6 min
5–6 oz380°F / 193°C8–10 minFlip not needed, baste once
8–10 oz, split in half380°F / 193°C10–12 minProbe the thickest half
Garlic butter finish380°F / 193°CLast 2 minSpoon over while cooking

The meat turns opaque and white as it cooks — that is the visual cue alongside the thermometer. Pull at 145°F / 63°C; the meat keeps a slight translucence near the shell even when done, so the thermometer decides.

Lemon butter and serving

Melted butter with a squeeze of lemon is the classic — the air fryer version needs no clarifying: two tablespoons of butter per tail, melted, with the paprika brushed on before cooking and the lemon at serving.

Serve immediately — lobster holds heat well but toughens as it sits in the hot shell. Rest it two minutes off the heat, then plate.

Five mistakes with air fryer lobster tail

  1. Cooking inside an uncut shell. The butterfly cut exposes the meat; an uncut shell steams unevenly.
  2. Overcooking past 145°F / 63°C. Lobster turns rubbery in minutes; pull at temperature.
  3. Skipping the thermometer. Translucent meat near the shell looks undercooked even when done.
  4. Boiling instead. Water washes out the flavor the air fryer concentrates.
  5. Letting it sit in the hot shell. Two minutes of rest, then plate — sitting toughens the meat.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a lobster tail take in an air fryer? 6–8 minutes at 380°F / 193°C for a 4-ounce butterflied tail, 8–10 minutes for 5–6 ounces. Verify the thickest part reaches 145°F / 63°C.

What temperature should lobster be inside? 145°F / 63°C — the FDA standard for shellfish, the same as fish. Pull at temperature; the meat turns rubbery past it.

Do I need to butterfly the tail? Yes — it is what exposes the meat to the hot air. A tail in an uncut shell steams unevenly.

Why is my lobster rubbery? It overcooked. Pull at 145°F / 63°C and plate after a two-minute rest — lobster toughens fast past temperature.

Can I cook frozen lobster tails? Thaw them first — overnight in the refrigerator. A frozen tail cooks unevenly and the thermometer reading becomes unreliable.

Lobster tail rewards the cut and the thermometer: butterfly, butter, 380°F / 193°C, pulled at 145°F / 63°C. Ten minutes later the fastest luxury in the air fryer is on the plate.

Always verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. Cooking times are starting points and vary by appliance model, wattage and basket size.

entry.title: Air Fryer Meal Prep Chart: What Batches Well and What Does Not
